name: application-nps-rating-scale
title: Rating Scale (NPS)
description: 0–10 Net Promoter Score rating row with real selectable state, colored by detractor (0–6), passive (7–8), or promoter (9–10) zone derived from the score itself.
useWhen: Running a Net Promoter Score survey ("How likely are you to recommend us?").
You want the detractor/passive/promoter zone coloring to update automatically from the selected score.
A single numeric 0–10 scale is the right input, not a star rating or emoji scale.
avoidWhen: You need a qualitative 1–5 satisfaction scale — use rating-input-emoji instead.
You're collecting a star rating for a product/service, not likelihood-to-recommend — use the rating component instead.
You need to aggregate and display many responses — use rating-distribution instead of this single-response input.
responsiveBehavior: The 11 buttons sit in a single row and shrink slightly on narrow viewports; wrap the row in a horizontal scroll container if space is very constrained.
accessibility: The scale is a real fieldset/legend with role='radiogroup' and each score as role='radio' with aria-checked.
Zone color is supplementary — the selected score's number remains visible as white-on-color text.
End labels ("Not at all likely" / "Extremely likely") are always visible text, not implied by position alone.

variants.title: Rating scale (NPS)
variants.description: 0–10 NPS scale with score 9 selected, showing the green promoter-zone color, on a light surface.
accessibility: Selected-state color and the score number both change together, so the selection is never conveyed by color alone.

variants.title: Rating scale (NPS) (Dark)
variants.description: The same 0–10 NPS scale with score 9 selected, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Zone colors must meet WCAG AA contrast against both the dark background and the white/dark selected text.
